overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to provide reasonable accommodations for mobility-aid users and by keeping inadequate minutes for its March 3 and March 10, 2012 meetings; the notice, closed-building, recording, and access-entrance and snow allegations were rejected.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the March 3 and March 10, 2012 notices listed topics ('FY13 Budgets', 'Special/Annual Town Meeting Articles') too vaguely.
allegations.key_passage: The notices for the Board's March 3, 2012 and March 10, 2012 meetings were sufficiently specific because they informed the public that the Board would be generally reviewing the Town budget for the upcoming year and the warrant for the upcoming Special and Annual Town Meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the March 3 and March 10, 2012 meetings were held on days when Town Hall was closed.
allegations.key_passage: While the Open Meeting Law does not prohibit a public body from holding a meeting on a day for which public buildings are closed,

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to video record and broadcast its March 3 and March 10, 2012 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: In addition, a public body is not required to make an audio or video recording of its meetings.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the March 3, 2012 meeting was held at a location whose handicapped accessible entrance was locked.
allegations.key_passage: We credit the Board's account, and do not find that the Board held a meeting at a location for which the handicapped entrance was locked, or failed to clear the parking lot of snow.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the municipal building parking lot was not plowed on March 3, 2012, making it hard for a wheelchair user to attend.
allegations.key_passage: We credit the Board's account, and do not find that the Board held a meeting at a location for which the handicapped entrance was locked, or failed to clear the parking lot of snow.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the March 3 and March 10, 2012 meetings were not accessible to people using mobility aids because a 24-hour advance accommodation request was required.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law on March 3, 2012 and March 10, 2012 by failing to provide reasonable accommodations to individuals who require mobility aids.

allegations.summary: Not alleged by complainant; the AG reviewed on its own whether the March 3 and March 10, 2012 minutes adequately summarized the discussions.
allegations.key_passage: A member of the public who was not in attendance at the meeting would not have a clear understanding of what occurred during the meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Amend the March 3, 2012 and March 10, 2012 meeting minutes, to the best of the Board's ability, to include a detailed summary of the discussions on each topic.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law. Additionally, we order that the Board amend its March 3, 2012 and March 10, 2012 meeting minutes to the best of its ability to include a detailed summary of the discussions on each topic.
